A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TRCE and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched reliably despite added appendix sections and renumbered figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original TRCE experiments on sexual-content and multi-concept erasure, component ablations, and artistic-style erasure, including results in Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative celebrity-erasure comparisons in Appendix E and qualitative experiments on newer diffusion architectures in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The core two-stage algorithm and objectives remain unchanged. Appendix E adds a celebrity-specific adaptation that trains cross-attention key/value matrices during stage two. Appendix F introduces encoder-only first-stage editing for SDXL, context_embedder editing for SD3/FLUX, and LoRA fine-tuning. These are targeted procedural extensions.

E1.justification: V2 retains the malicious-content and artistic-style tasks and adds selective celebrity-identity erasure using MACE's benchmark of 100 erased and 100 retained celebrities. This substantially extends task coverage to portrait protection and preservation of unrelated identities. Artistic-style erasure was already present in v1.

E2.justification: AdvUnlearn is newly evaluated in the sexual-erasure comparison in Table 1 and the corresponding qualitative comparisons. Comparator membership in the retained multi-concept and artistic-style quantitative experiments is unchanged. The new celebrity experiment uses already represented methods: UCE, RECE, and MACE.

E3.justification: V2 adds FID_real against real COCO images alongside the retained original-model-reference FID, renamed FID_gen. It introduces a celebrity evaluation protocol using GIPHY detection, erase/retain accuracies, and their harmonic mean, plus SDXL/SD3/FLUX experimental configurations. A beta=1 control extends the guidance ablation. Existing benchmark prompt counts and the original SD1.4 training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 5 and 8 add the same no-guidance-enhancement control, extending the existing loss and guidance-scale analyses. Appendix F adds qualitative architecture-compatibility checks, and the expanded visualization appendix supplies additional preservation and multi-concept cases. The original stage, token, and concept-augmentation ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2 continues reporting point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds FID_real scores, AdvUnlearn results, celebrity-erasure results, and qualitative outputs. Existing scores also change: SD1.4's P4D ASR changes from 84.00% to 83.44% in Table 1; Table 2 changes SLD's overall inappropriate rate from 35.6% to 20.8% and MACE's original-model-reference FID from 56.33 to 19.31. These are reported revisions; the PDFs do not establish whether they reflect corrections or reruns.

T1.justification: The existing mathematical formulation, closed-form solution, objectives, and equations 1–10 remain unchanged. The new equation 11 states the standard harmonic mean adopted for celebrity evaluation. It adds metric documentation without introducing new theoretical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about two-stage malicious-concept erasure, EoT-based semantic mapping, trajectory steering, and knowledge preservation. The additional experiments support broader applicability without redefining these principal contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 newly explains why FID_gen is preferred for assessing knowledge preservation. Appendix E explains the celebrity-specific layer choice through shared portrait structure, while Appendix F discusses architectural compatibility and restricting SDXL editing to reduce cost and capacity disruption. Section 5.4 also adds an explicit interpretation of the guidance-enhancement control.

D1.justification: V2 documents five trajectories per celebrity, the celebrity-specific trainable layers, and model-specific editing locations and LoRA use. Original SD1.4 implementation details and the code-access statement remain. However, v1's explicit disclosure of 3,000 generated images for FID disappears, and v2 supplies no replacement sample count.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for FLUX.1-dev, the GIPHY Celebrity Detector, and a 2025 survey of attacks and defenses on text-to-image diffusion models. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged. AdvUnlearn's paper was already in v1's bibliography.

P1.justification: Changes include localized rewrites of metric explanations and second-stage ablation discussion, new appendix sections E and F, relocation of the visualization section from E to G, and added acknowledgements. The principal narrative, section order, and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands substantially through the celebrity table and figure, architecture-transfer illustrations, and a new multi-concept image grid. Existing comparison tables gain metric or control columns, and qualitative grids add AdvUnlearn and additional preservation examples. V1 Figures 9–10 become expanded Figures 11–12 in v2; they are retained rather than removed.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical assessment through the AdvUnlearn comparison, complementary FID references, quantified celebrity erasure, and a direct guidance-enhancement control. These make the evidence more informative while retaining the established core contribution. The net gain is limited by unexplained revisions to existing scores, removal of FID sample-count details, and qualitative-only support for compatibility with newer architectures.
